findings.summary: Two of the brief's own decisions have no worked-example line. One is that a call with no completion counts as having run. The other is that the check runs whatever the session's exit. The likely implementation would silently skip the second for a killed session. Runner.Run returns early, before any Output reaches the caller, when Parse finds no result event, and a timed-out Copilot session is killed before it prints one. If the calls are gathered in Parse or carried on Result after that point, a timed-out session is never re-judged, and no gate notices.
findings.evidence: internal/driver/session.go:433-436: `out, ok := ad.Parse(...)`, then `if !ok { ...; return res, nil }`, before res is filled. internal/driver/agent_copilot.go Parse: `if !result { return Output{}, false }`. The stub already has STUB_SILENT=1, which prints no result event (cmd/vloop/run_harness_test.go:106). No line of the worked example uses it, and none has a start without a completion.
findings.fix: Add two worked-example lines, each a named test. (a) Phase work, STUB_SILENT=1 and STUB_EXIT non-zero, with a bash `git push` start and its completion: FENCE BYPASSED work, exit 9. (b) A bash `git push` tool.execution_start with no tool.execution_complete: FENCE BYPASSED, exit 9. Say in F1 that the calls are read from the session's stdout even when it holds no result event.

findings.summary: `run.second-review on` is not a value of run.second-review. A test author has to guess one. Two of the modes, on-pass and both-pass, only run the second review when the primary review passes.
findings.evidence: internal/config/config.go:37: SecondReviewModes = off, record, feedback, on-pass, both-pass. internal/driver/iterate.go:898: `(mode == "on-pass" || mode == "both-pass") && primary != "PASS"` skips the second review.
findings.fix: Write `run.second-review = "record"` (or name the mode and say the primary review passes).

findings.summary: F1 does not say whether the per-call stderr lines are masked, or whether they also go to the run log as the REFS MOVED lines do (t.warn / it.warn: masked and logged). Copilot's file tools pass absolute paths, so `<what>` will usually be a path under $HOME. F2 says its path is `unmasked`; F1 says nothing. Two sessions could implement it two ways, and a line that reaches the run log unmasked breaks the repository's rule 2.
findings.evidence: internal/driver/iterate.go:136-141 (warn masks, then logs and prints). internal/driver/plan.go:552-556 (REFS MOVED lines through t.warn). CLAUDE.md rule 2. In tools/agent-eval/testdata/observed/copilot-events.jsonl, file tools take `path`. The worked example's lines carry no path, so no test settles this.
findings.fix: State it, for example: `printed through the phase's warning line (masked, and in the run log), as REFS MOVED's lines are`. Optionally add a worked-example line with a `create` to a path outside the repository in a review phase, showing the masked `~/…` form.

findings.summary: The phrase `after its sentence on the git keys it gains `, or a Copilot session ran …`` has an unclear insertion point. The cell reads `…or the git hooks; nothing was committed. The message names the key`. The insert begins with a comma, so it only reads right straight after `or the git hooks`, yet `after its sentence` suggests after the full stop.
findings.fix: Write `after `or the git hooks`` (before `; nothing was committed`).

decisions: Re-judge every call from the JSON Lines rather than match a hook log. Sound: a log would sit where a bypassing session could write it.
Reuse exit 9 rather than charge an attempt or add a new code. Sound: the meaning is the same, a guard tripped.

Accepted risk: a Copilot tool that never calls the hook (report_intent is the candidate) would halt every run, and no setting turns the check off. Evidence: 140 calls in 7 sessions, 0 false halts. Round 2 checked this against data outside the repository. Worth the operator knowing that the only way back is a code change.
Hash the hook binary before and after the session (F2) rather than run a one-off probe.
A call with no completion counts as having run, and the check runs whatever the session's exit.
The re-judge applies the hook's own rule (bash or powershell with an empty command is denied) before the judge.

Nothing is reverted after FENCE BYPASSED or HOOK CHANGED beyond what each phase already restores. A plan session's out-of-state changes stay, because the halt comes before revertTree. The operator decides.
HOOK CHANGED prints the binary's path unmasked.
The check lives in vloop's phases, not in Runner.Run, so tools/agent-eval sessions are never halted.
